mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates stronger labor market conditions, which typically support corporate earnings growth and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of weak industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and strong housing starts (HOUST > 1700) indicates a resilient consumer sector amid supply constraints, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (INDPRO < 100 AND HOUST > 1700) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances (i.e., positive returns occur in <= 60% of cases) or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 6.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain aggressive tightening, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL exceeds 6.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) reflect robust consumer demand for residential construction, which typically signals a strong economy and supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 60-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls exceeding 200,000 jobs signals strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth exceeds 200,000 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is rising (FEDFUNDS > 0.5% change from previous month) and the unemployment rate is falling (UNRATE < 0.3% change from previous month), it indicates a tight labor market with aggressive monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market strength
failure_condition: The interaction condition (FEDFUNDS change > 0.5% AND UNRATE change < -0.3%) fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances (i.e., negative returns occur in <= 60% of cases) or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) following a supply shock, the economy faces reduced output capacity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate profits are pressured.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls below 100 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below -0.03.
